name: MioIsland

hlido_opinion.headline: A narrow, well-executed macOS utility that turns the MacBook notch into a live control surface for Claude Code sessions — approve a diff without switching windows — with an iPhone companion and the code on GitHub.
hlido_opinion.body: MioIsland solves a small, specific and genuinely annoying problem: when you run several coding-agent sessions at once, the cost is not the agents, it is the window-switching required to notice that one of them is waiting on you. It puts that status where your eyes already are. The collapsed notch shows status dots per session with a colour code (cyan working, green done, red error) and the project name; expanded, it lists running sessions with status, tool calls and duration; and when Claude Code asks for permission, the diff renders in the notch with green/red highlighting so you can approve or deny in place. That last feature is the one that justifies the product — approval is the step that actually blocks an agent, and removing a context switch from it is a real saving rather than a novelty. The surface is concrete in the ways that matter: an interactive demo, a named monitoring model, specific session states, an iPhone companion with documented pairing, a GitHub repository, and a direct download. The scope is honestly narrow and the page does not pretend otherwise. Limits are equally clear. This is macOS-only and, by its central conceit, notch-hardware-only — it will not help on an external display or an older MacBook. It is a monitoring and approval layer over an agent someone else makes, so its usefulness is wholly contingent on Claude Code's behaviour and interfaces continuing to suit it, and the page states no compatibility policy for that dependency. No version, licence, release history or user count was captured, so maintenance durability is unknown for a tool that sits in the permission path of an agent editing your code. The surface also mixes English and Chinese inconsistently.

tier_rationale: STEADY (71) because the product is focused, the core feature (approve an agent's diff in the notch without switching windows) is a real workflow saving, and it is demonstrated concretely with a download, a GitHub repository and an iPhone companion. It is held back by hard platform limits (macOS plus notch hardware), total dependency on another vendor's agent with no stated compatibility policy, and no visible version, licence or adoption evidence.
what_it_does_well: Removes a context switch from the step that actually blocks an agent — rendering the permission diff in the notch for one-click approve or deny
Legible at-a-glance status: colour-coded session dots, project name, tool calls and duration without opening anything
Handles multiple concurrent agent sessions as the normal case rather than an edge case
iPhone companion with documented pairing, extending monitoring away from the desk
Source on GitHub and a direct download — the product is inspectable, not just described
An interactive demo on the page rather than a static screenshot
what_it_fails_at: macOS-only, and dependent on notch hardware by its central design — useless on an external display or an older MacBook
Entirely dependent on Claude Code's interfaces and behaviour, with no stated compatibility or support policy for that dependency
No version, licence, release history or changelog captured
No user count, star figure or adoption evidence on the reviewed surface
Inconsistent bilingual surface, with Chinese strings appearing inside an otherwise English page
It sits in the approval path of an agent editing your code, and says nothing about what happens to that path if it crashes or is not running
best_for: MacBook users running several Claude Code sessions at once who lose time to window-switching
Developers who want agent approvals surfaced without leaving the current window
Anyone who wants to glance at agent status while working in another app
not_recommended_for: Anyone not on a notch-equipped MacBook, including external-display setups
Teams using agents other than Claude Code — nothing else is supported on the captured surface
Users who need a licensed, versioned, supported tool in their agent approval path
red_flags: A utility that intermediates approvals for an agent editing your code, with no stated version, licence or failure behaviour on the reviewed surface
Single-vendor dependency on Claude Code with no compatibility commitment — an upstream interface change can disable the product outright

compared_to.verdict_diff: Claude Code is the agent; MioIsland is a macOS surface for watching and approving it. They are complements, not alternatives — MioIsland has no value without it.

Cursor keeps agent approvals inside the IDE you are already in; MioIsland keeps them in the notch so you can be anywhere on the machine. Choose Cursor if you live in one editor, MioIsland if your agents run in terminals while you work elsewhere.
opencode is a terminal agent you would run and watch yourself; MioIsland adds a monitoring layer but only for Claude Code. Different layers of the same workflow.

agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: MioIsland is a human-facing monitoring and approval surface over another agent, not something an agent calls. It consumes Claude Code session state and presents it to a person; no API, CLI, SDK or MCP endpoint is advertised for other agents to drive it. Its relevance to agent work is high, but as an operator's instrument rather than an integration target.
